function: Joint receive beamforming and per-round power control for over-the-air aggregation of federated models in cell-free MIMO, minimizing the optimality gap under a long-term power constraint (pp. 1-4).
system: Cell-free MIMO uplink: 6 APs with 4 antennas each, 3 single-antenna UEs, 500 m x 500 m, 2.4 GHz, 20 MHz; no RIS (p. 4).
method: Closed-form MOP receive beamformer and Lyapunov power control (LOFPC); no trained PHY network; the learned element is the FL model (local SGD) aggregated over the air (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh small-scale fading with log-distance urban path loss; synthetic ridge-regression task, q=10, 1000 samples per UE; no external dataset or measurement (p. 4).
test_conditions: Single configuration: 3 UEs, 6 APs, 4 antennas, 2.4 GHz; loss versus rounds and penalty V; no other scenario or setup tested (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Fixed power, channel-inversion (Ci), Lagrangian offline power (Lgr) of [11], MRC beamforming per [8], combined with MOP or MRC, plus a perfect-aggregation reference (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Loss function versus communication rounds and versus penalty V; average power versus rounds against the long-term budget (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "the small-scale fading follows a Rayleigh fading model"; the channel is a custom Rayleigh and log-distance simulator, with no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel, so the criterion is not met.
q2_support: p. 4: "randomly placing 3 UEs and 6 APs"; a single configuration is simulated, and no other number of UEs, APs or antennas, band or scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "Fixed power strategy: Each user employs a fixed transmission power in each communication round"; p. 5: "to solve the time coupling issue arising from long-term power constraints (13) in power control problem [11]"; p. 5: "The two LOFPC algorithms consistently outperform both the fixed and Lgr algorithm".
q4_support: p. 4: "To reduce the complexity of handling (13) within a finite time"; this is the only mention of complexity and it is qualitative, so no order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime is reported anywhere in the paper.
q5_support: p. 4: "We adopt the ridge regression task setup as described"; the data are generated samples of a synthetic learning task and the channels come from a custom simulator, with no code or data link or DOI in the paper.
notes: Passes no_learning only through the OTA-FL rule: the method is classical optimization (closed-form MOP beamformer, Lyapunov power control), and the learned element is the FL model trained across the UEs (p. 2). Area 7 because the problem solved is the over-the-air aggregation itself (pp. 2-4). Not single-antenna: APs have 4 antennas (p. 4). q3 is met through the Lgr power control of [11] (p. 5) and the MRC combiner referenced to [8] (p. 5), both adapted by the authors to this setting, so the reviewer should confirm that they count as earlier published aggregation designs; the fixed and Ci powers are heuristics defined by the paper. The PDF is arXiv 2410.05354v3 of 23 Oct 2024 and prints no DOI; its title and first authors match the Crossref record of the DOI.
